resources.string: A: uptake from the starting amount
B: uptake from what remains after A

This bookkeeping model follows an already dissolved generic nutrient through two representative small-intestinal segments in sequence. Both stages represent combined uptake across a segment, not a measured rate for a single enterocyte. A and B do not stand for named anatomical regions. The percentages are invented, not reference values. The model ignores digestion, transit time, and what happens after absorption; it does not predict real uptake.

Let a and b be the slider percentages divided by 100. For a starting amount M, A absorbs M × a and B absorbs M × (1 − a) × b. The plot shows the sum as a percentage of M. The amount left in the lumen is M × (1 − a) × (1 − b).
Still in the lumen after B: %1$s%% of the starting amount
